title: Choose an array size at run time
summary: Fortran: Choose an array size at run time. Allocate four positions.
introduction: An allocatable array gets its size when allocate runs. deallocate releases its storage.
learningObjectives: Choose an array size at run time with Fortran

blocks.text: Install GNU Fortran. Save each example as lesson.f90, run gfortran -std=f2008 lesson.f90 -o lesson, then run it.
Choose an array size at run time

blocks.title: Choose an array size at run time
blocks.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer, allocatable :: scores(:)
allocate(scores(3))
scores = 0
write(*,'(I0)') size(scores)
deallocate(scores)
end program lesson

blocks.text: allocate creates three positions. size reads that count before deallocate releases them.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Allocate before using the array and do not use it after deallocation.
